title.de: Das Passiv: is baked, was built
title.it: Il passivo: is baked, was built

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj se dela ali je bilo narejeno, ko ni pomembno, kdo (The bread is baked here, The bridge was built in 1720), z by, če je pomembno, in s can be.
goal.de: Du sagst, was gemacht wird oder gemacht wurde, ohne zu sagen, wer es tut (The bread is baked here, The bridge was built in 1720), mit by, wer es war, und mit can be.
goal.it: Dici che cosa si fa o è stato fatto, senza dire chi (The bread is baked here, The bridge was built in 1720), con by per dire chi, e con can be.
goal.en: You can say what is done or was done, without saying who (The bread is baked here, The bridge was built in 1720), with by for who did it, and with can be.

say.sl: Ko je pomembno, kaj se zgodi, ne kdo to naredi, rabiš **is, are** + deležnik: **The bread is baked here.** (Kruh pečejo tukaj.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** (Jajca prodajajo na kmetiji.) Temu se reče trpnik. Kdo peče, tu ni pomembno. Slovenščina reče *pečejo* ali *se peče*.
say.de: Ist wichtig, was geschieht, nicht wer es tut, nimmst du **is, are** + Partizip: **The bread is baked here.** (Das Brot wird hier gebacken.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** (Eier werden auf dem Hof verkauft.) Das ist das Passiv. Vorsicht: *wird* heißt hier **is**, nicht *will*.
say.it: Quando conta che cosa succede, non chi lo fa, usi **is, are** + participio: **The bread is baked here.** (Qui si fa il pane.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** (Le uova si vendono alla fattoria.) È il passivo. L'italiano dice *si fa* o *viene fatto*.
say.en: When what happens matters more than who does it, use **is, are** + the participle: **The bread is baked here.** **Eggs are sold at the farm.** This is the passive. Who bakes the bread doesn't matter here.

examples.en: Eggs are sold at the farm.
examples.de: Eier werden auf dem Hof verkauft.
examples.it: Le uova si vendono alla fattoria.

say.sl: Za preteklost rabiš **was, were** + deležnik: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Most so zgradili leta 1720.) **The letters were sent yesterday.** (Pisma so poslali včeraj.) **The Lake District was made a national park in 1951.** En: was, več: were.
say.de: Für die Vergangenheit nimmst du **was, were** + Partizip: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Die Brücke wurde 1720 gebaut.) **The letters were sent yesterday.** (Die Briefe wurden gestern abgeschickt.) **The Lake District was made a national park in 1951.** Eines: was, mehrere: were.
say.it: Per il passato usi **was, were** + participio: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Il ponte fu costruito nel 1720.) **The letters were sent yesterday.** (Le lettere sono state spedite ieri.) **The Lake District was made a national park in 1951.** Uno: was, più di uno: were.
say.en: For the past use **was, were** + the participle: **The bridge was built in 1720.** **The letters were sent yesterday.** **The Lake District was made a national park in 1951.** One: was, more than one: were.

say.sl: Deležnik je pri pravilnih glagolih **-ed** (baked, mended), drugi imajo svojega: **built, made, sold, sent, kept, written, taken, stolen, broken, given**. Ni preteklik: **was written**, ne wrote. Ljudje rečejo tudi *It was broke*, *It was took*; pisava hoče **broken**, **taken**. V govoru je pravilno tudi **got**: **My van got stolen.** (Ukradli so mi kombi.)
say.de: Das Partizip ist bei regelmäßigen Verben **-ed** (baked, mended), die anderen haben ein eigenes: **built, made, sold, sent, kept, written, taken, stolen, broken, given**. Es ist nicht die Vergangenheit: **was written**, nicht wrote. Man sagt auch *It was broke*, *It was took*; geschrieben steht **broken**, **taken**. Gesprochen ist auch **got** richtig: **My van got stolen.** (Mein Lieferwagen wurde gestohlen.)
say.it: Il participio è **-ed** per i verbi regolari (baked, mended), gli altri ne hanno uno loro: **built, made, sold, sent, kept, written, taken, stolen, broken, given**. Non è il passato: **was written**, non wrote. Si dice anche *It was broke*, *It was took*; per iscritto si usa **broken**, **taken**. A voce va bene anche **got**: **My van got stolen.** (Mi hanno rubato il furgone.)
say.en: The participle is **-ed** for regular verbs (baked, mended); the others have their own: **built, made, sold, sent, kept, written, taken, stolen, broken, given**. It isn't the past: **was written**, not wrote. People also say *It was broke*, *It was took*; writing wants **broken**, **taken**. In talk **got** is right too: **My van got stolen.**

say.sl: Kdo je to naredil, pove **by**: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Vrata je popravil gospod Dixon.) **This honey is made by Arthur's bees.** Slovenščina tu pogosto samo obrne stavek. Če ni pomembno ali je jasno, kdo, **by** izpustiš: **The inn was built in 1750.** Najprej to, kar je znano, novo na koncu.
say.de: Wer es getan hat, sagt **by**, wo Deutsch *von* sagt: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Das Tor wurde von Mr Dixon repariert.) **This honey is made by Arthur's bees.** Nicht *from*. Ist es nicht wichtig oder klar, wer, fällt **by** weg: **The inn was built in 1750.**
say.it: Chi l'ha fatto lo dice **by**, dove l'italiano dice *da*: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Il cancello è stato riparato da Mr Dixon.) **This honey is made by Arthur's bees.** Se non conta o è chiaro chi, **by** resta fuori: **The inn was built in 1750.**
say.en: **by** says who did it: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** **This honey is made by Arthur's bees.** If it doesn't matter, or it's clear who, leave **by** out: **The inn was built in 1750.**

say.sl: Vprašanje in zanikanje naredi be, brez do in did: **Was the letter sent?** (So pismo poslali?) **Is the bread baked here?** **When was the bridge built?** (Kdaj so zgradili most?) **The gate wasn't closed.** (Vrata niso bila zaprta.) **The eggs aren't sold on Sundays.**
say.de: Frage und Verneinung macht be, ohne do und did: **Was the letter sent?** (Wurde der Brief abgeschickt?) **Is the bread baked here?** **When was the bridge built?** (Wann wurde die Brücke gebaut?) **The gate wasn't closed.** (Das Tor wurde nicht geschlossen.) **The eggs aren't sold on Sundays.**
say.it: Domanda e negazione le fa be, senza do e did: **Was the letter sent?** (La lettera è stata spedita?) **Is the bread baked here?** **When was the bridge built?** (Quando fu costruito il ponte?) **The gate wasn't closed.** (Il cancello non è stato chiuso.) **The eggs aren't sold on Sundays.**
say.en: be asks and says no, with no do or did: **Was the letter sent?** **Is the bread baked here?** **When was the bridge built?** **The gate wasn't closed.** **The eggs aren't sold on Sundays.**

examples.it: Il cancello non è stato chiuso.

say.sl: Po **can** in **must** pride **be** + deležnik: **The gate can be opened from inside.** (Vrata se dajo odpreti od znotraj.) **Cheese can be kept for a month.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.** (Pse je treba voditi na povodcu.) Tako pišejo na napisih. Zanikanje: **can't be**, **mustn't be**.
say.de: Nach **can** und **must** kommt **be** + Partizip: **The gate can be opened from inside.** (Das Tor kann von innen geöffnet werden.) **Cheese can be kept for a month.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.** (Hunde müssen an der Leine geführt werden.) So steht es auf Schildern. Verneint: **can't be**, **mustn't be**.
say.it: Dopo **can** e **must** viene **be** + participio: **The gate can be opened from inside.** (Il cancello si può aprire da dentro.) **Cheese can be kept for a month.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.** (I cani devono essere tenuti al guinzaglio.) Così si legge sui cartelli. Al negativo: **can't be**, **mustn't be**.
say.en: After **can** and **must** comes **be** + the participle: **The gate can be opened from inside.** **Cheese can be kept for a month.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.** That's how notices say it. With no: **can't be**, **mustn't be**.

exercises.text: The Packhorse is very old. It ___ built in 1750. Today its bread ___ baked in the kitchen, and the eggs ___ brought from Jack's farm. Last year the roof ___ mended, and all the windows ___ painted.

translation.sl: Packhorse je zelo star. Zgradili so ga leta 1750. Danes pečejo kruh v kuhinji, jajca pa prinašajo z Jackove kmetije. Lani so popravili streho in prepleskali vsa okna.
translation.de: Das Packhorse ist sehr alt. Es wurde 1750 gebaut. Heute wird sein Brot in der Küche gebacken, und die Eier werden von Jacks Hof gebracht. Letztes Jahr wurde das Dach repariert, und alle Fenster wurden gestrichen.
translation.it: Il Packhorse è molto vecchio. Fu costruito nel 1750. Oggi il pane si fa in cucina e le uova si portano dalla fattoria di Jack. L'anno scorso è stato riparato il tetto e sono state dipinte tutte le finestre.
translation.en: The Packhorse is very old. It was built in 1750. Today its bread is baked in the kitchen, and the eggs are brought from Jack's farm. Last year the roof was mended, and all the windows were painted.

translation.sl: Napis na kmetiji: Pse je treba voditi na povodcu. Vrata se dajo odpreti od znotraj, a jih je treba za seboj zapreti. Vozovnic tukaj ni mogoče kupiti. Sinoči so Samu ukradli kombi s parkirišča!
translation.de: Schild auf dem Hof: Hunde müssen an der Leine geführt werden. Das Tor kann von innen geöffnet werden, muss aber hinter dir geschlossen werden. Karten können hier nicht gekauft werden. Gestern Abend wurde Sams Lieferwagen vom Parkplatz gestohlen!
translation.it: Cartello alla fattoria: i cani devono essere tenuti al guinzaglio. Il cancello si può aprire da dentro, ma va chiuso dopo il passaggio. Qui non si possono comprare biglietti. Ieri sera a Sam hanno rubato il furgone dal parcheggio!
translation.en: Notice at the farm: Dogs must be kept on a lead. The gate can be opened from inside, but it must be closed after you. Tickets can't be bought here. Last night Sam's van was stolen from the car park!

exercises.text: The cheese ___ made on Jack's farm. It ___ taken to Keswick by van. Last week the van ___ stolen! The next day two men ___ seen near the bridge. The van ___ found the same night, and it wasn't even dirty.

translation.sl: Sir delajo na Jackovi kmetiji. V Keswick ga vozijo s kombijem. Prejšnji teden so kombi ukradli! Naslednji dan so pri mostu videli dva moža. Kombi so našli še isto noč in še umazan ni bil.
translation.de: Der Käse wird auf Jacks Hof gemacht. Er wird mit dem Lieferwagen nach Keswick gebracht. Letzte Woche wurde der Lieferwagen gestohlen! Am nächsten Tag wurden zwei Männer bei der Brücke gesehen. Der Lieferwagen wurde noch in derselben Nacht gefunden, und er war nicht einmal schmutzig.
translation.it: Il formaggio si fa alla fattoria di Jack. Viene portato a Keswick con il furgone. La settimana scorsa il furgone è stato rubato! Il giorno dopo sono stati visti due uomini vicino al ponte. Il furgone è stato ritrovato la notte stessa, e non era nemmeno sporco.
translation.en: The cheese is made on Jack's farm. It is taken to Keswick by van. Last week the van was stolen! The next day two men were seen near the bridge. The van was found the same night, and it wasn't even dirty.
